title: Bug Hunt 3 - Word Finder (off-by-one binary search)
body:
Goal: fix the 2 off-by-one bugs in find_word. When it works, Run prints:

apple -> 0
dragon -> 3
lemon -> 11
zebra -> -1

How to hunt:

  1. Press Run. Which words are found, which are not?
  2. Do a trace table on paper for find_word(["ant", "bee", "cat"], "ant"): write low, high and mid for every loop. Why is "ant" not found?
  3. Click Debug and step through the same search. Does the Variables view match your table?

Hint: the last index of a list with 12 items is not 12. And when low and high are equal, there is still ONE word left to check.

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Run it and see which words are found and which are not. Then look at the lines that set up the search, just before the loop and at the top of the loop. Think about the very last word in the list.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: Counting from 0, a list of 3 items has indexes 0, 1 and 2. Write a trace table on paper for ["ant", "bee", "cat"] and "ant". Add columns for low, high and mid, and fill in one row per loop.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Look at the starting value of high. Counting from 0, is it the index of the last word? Then think about the loop condition. When low and high are the same number, is there still one word left to look at? Try your trace table again after each change.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Bug Hunt 3: Word Finder
# find_word uses binary search on a sorted list of words.
# It has 2 off-by-one bugs. Some words are never found - and if you fix only
# one bug, it may even crash with an IndexError!
# Expected output when fixed:
#   apple -> 0
#   dragon -> 3
#   lemon -> 11
#   zebra -> -1

WORDS = ["apple", "banana", "cherry", "dragon", "eagle", "falcon",
         "guitar", "harbor", "island", "jungle", "koala", "lemon"]


def find_word(words, target):
    """Binary search in a SORTED list. Return the index of target, or -1."""
    low = 0
    high = len(words)
    while low < high:
        mid = (low + high) // 2
        if words[mid] == target:
            return mid
        elif words[mid] < target:
            low = mid + 1
        else:
            high = mid - 1
    return -1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for word in ["apple", "dragon", "lemon", "zebra"]:
        print(word, "->", find_word(WORDS, word))
